predecessors.name: British Raj
predecessors.text: the Dominion of India of 15 August 1947: 'In 1947, the British Indian Empire was partitioned' into Hindu-majority India and Muslim-majority Pakistan; the frontier tracts that became the NEFA are…

ledger.x: 15 August 1947: the Dominion of India is born as British India is partitioned.
22-27 October 1947: the first Kashmir war begins.
26 October 1947: Jammu and Kashmir accedes to India.
November 1947: India takes over Junagadh.
13-18 September 1948: Operation Polo ends the Nizam's rule.
1 January 1949: the UN-mediated ceasefire ends the Kashmir war.
August 1949: India returns Dewangiri to Bhutan with the Treaty of Friendship.
1950: Sikkim becomes an Indian protectorate.
26 January 1950: the Dominion becomes the Republic of India.
2 May 1950: Chandernagore passes from France to India.
February 1951: India takes the Tawang tract from Tibet.
1 November 1954: Pondicherry passes to India.
1961: Dadra and Nagar Haveli become a Union Territory of India.
17 December 1961: Operation Vijay begins.
19 December 1961: Portugal surrenders Goa.
December 1961: Goa, Daman and Diu join India.
20 October 1962: China attacks along the border.
21 November 1962: the guns fall silent.
5 August 1965: Pakistani infiltrators cross the Line of Control in Kashmir.
10 January 1966: the Tashkent Declaration.
1968: the Kutch tribunal awards part of the Rann to Pakistan.
3 December 1971: India enters the war in East Pakistan.
16 December 1971: Pakistan surrenders in Dhaka.
1974: Kachchatheevu passes to Sri Lanka.
16 May 1975: Sikkim ends its protectorate status by merging with India.
16 May 1975: Sikkim becomes India's 22nd state.
13 April 1984: India occupies the Siachen Glacier region.
13 April 1984: the Siachen conflict begins.
3 May 1999: shepherds report a Pakistani intrusion in the Kargil district.
26 July 1999: the fighting ceases.
25 November 2003: the Siachen ceasefire.

wars.name: Indo-Pakistani war of 1947-1948
wars.outcome: Stalemate on the page ('Numerous analysts state that the war ended in a stalemate'); India kept about two-thirds of the princely state, Pakistan the west and the north (Azad Kashmir, Gilgit, Baltistan).

wars.name: Operation Polo
wars.outcome: Indian troops took complete control between 13 and 18 September 1948 (paraphrased); Hyderabad ceased to be a state.

wars.name: Annexation of Goa
wars.outcome: Indian victory in two days; Goa, Daman and Diu became a union territory in December 1961.

wars.name: Sino-Indian War
wars.outcome: Chinese victory; 'Status quo ante bellum' on the page's infobox, China withdrawing to the Line of Actual Control.

wars.name: Indo-Pakistani war of 1965
wars.outcome: Stalemate with the ground returned: Pakistan accepted the ceasefire on 23 September 1965 (UN resolution 20 September); the Tashkent Declaration of 10 January 1966 agreed to withdraw 'to pre-August lines no later than 25 February 1966'.

wars.name: Bangladesh Liberation War
wars.outcome: 'Bangladeshi-Indian victory': Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 and East Pakistan became Bangladesh; India annexed no land.

wars.name: Siachen conflict
wars.outcome: Indian victory: India holds the Saltoro Ridge heights (about 2,500 km2); ceasefire 25 November 2003.

wars.name: Kargil War
wars.outcome: Indian victory on the infobox, territorial result 'Status quo ante bellum': Pakistani forces held 130-200 km2 of heights in the Kargil district from May until the fighting ceased on 26 July 1999.

certainty.note: The princely states are acceding or being absorbed, the Kashmir front moves until the ceasefire of 1 January 1949, and the Hyderabad border is that of the Nizam's dominions; only the Radcliffe Line frontiers (Bengal, Punjab) are fixed.
Treaty and survey frontiers with Pakistan (Radcliffe Line, 1947), Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar.
